messages.subject: tooltip with two layers
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Is there a way of restricting a tooltip to a specific layer?

e.g. the code below produces a tooltip when both the line and the points are being hovered over.

In principle, this would be OK, but in this example, when hovering over the line, a constant value of 0.37 is given (the value of y for x = 1).

Ideally, I only want a tooltip when a point is hovered over.

```R
> set.seed(101)
>
> df <- data.frame(
>   x = 1:10,
>   y = round(runif(10), 2)
> )
>
> yval <- function(df) sprintf("y value: %s", df$y)
>
> ggvis(df, props(~x, ~y)) +
>   layer_point() +
>   layer_line() +
>   tooltip(yval)
```

Cheers,

Guy

messages.subject: Using brush_tooltip - does some 'reference' to brush need to be made in props()?
messages.subject_clean: Using brush_tooltip - does some 'reference' to brush need to be made in props()?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I was having problems with the brush tooltip, and have boiled it down to the following I think.

Could someone explain why the first two plots print output to the console when using the brush tooltip, whereas the third doesn't?

> under_the_hood <- function(x) {
>   print(str(x))
>   print(x)
> }
>
> base_plot <- ggvis(mtcars, props(x = ~wt, y = ~mpg))
>
> # plot 1
          # reference made to brush in props()
> base_plot +
>   layer_point(props(size.brush := 400)) +
>   brush_tooltip(under_the_hood)
>
> # plot 2
          # reference made to brush in props()
> base_plot +
>   layer_point(props(fillOpacity.brush := 0.1)) +
>   brush_tooltip(under_the_hood)
>
> # plot 3
          # no reference made to brush in props()
> base_plot +
>   layer_point() +
>   brush_tooltip(under_the_hood)

Cheers,

Guy

messages.subject: linked_brush philosophy
messages.body_plain:
Hi again ggvis team,

I am having great fun working with linked_brush() between scatterplots.

The fun then turned to experimentation, as I tried to make a link between a scatterplot and a histogram.

The goal was to brush a scatterplot and to have the bars of the histogram (or proper proportion thereof) respond in kind.

A further goal was to be able to brush the histogram and show the corresponding points on the scatterplot.

It didn't go well, as I'm pretty sure I'm not supposed to be able to do this (yet).

My guess is that the transform_bin() us getting in the way, and it doesn't help that there is not a one-to-one correspondence between the marks of the histogram and the marks of the scatterplot.

Anyhow, could this be something we might imagine being able to do in the future (or even to have linked_brush() among histograms of different variables representing the same dataframe)?

Thanks as always for entertaining my crazy questions,

Ian

messages.subject: Brushing with modifiable data sets
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have a multi-column data set, for which the user can specify two columns to be plotted via two selectInput controls.
I would like the plot to be brushable, but it doesn't seem to work with the selectInputs.

Fixing the columns to be plotted seem to be fine, as in the ggvis examples.

For now, the linked_brush object is given explicitly, but I would like to be able to have the linked_brush be reactive as well, so that it depends on the size of testdata but I have never managed to get that to work (I have tried wrapping it with a reactive() and reactiveValues() and using isolate().)

Here's the code I'm using at the moment:

server.r
> library(ggvis)
> shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
>
>   testdata <- reactive({
>
>     data <- data.frame(one   = rnorm(n = 1000, mean = 1),
>                        two   = rnorm(n = 1000, mean = 2),
>                        three = rnorm(n = 1000, mean = 3))
>
>     return(data)
>   })
>
>   output$selectInputGv1X <- renderUI({
>     if (is.na <http://is.na>(testdata())) {
>       return(NULL)
>     } else {
>       selectInput(inputId = "gv1X",
>                   label   = "x-axis",
>                   choices = names(testdata()))
>     }
>   })
>
>   output$selectInputGv1Y <- renderUI({
>     if (is.na <http://is.na>(testdata())) {
>       return(NULL)
>     } else {
>       selectInput(inputId = "gv1Y",
>                   label   = "y-axis",
>                   choices = names(testdata()))
>     }
>   })
>
>   lb <- linked_brush(keys = 1:1000)
>
>   gv1 <- reactive({
>     if (is.null(input$gv1X) | is.null(input$gv1Y)) {
>       ggvis()
>     } else {
>       ggvis(testdata, props(x = as.formula( paste("~", input$gv1X)),
>                             y = as.formula( paste("~", input$gv1Y))
>       )) +
>         layer_point(props(fill := lb$fill_prop(), fillOpacity := 0.8,
>                           fill.brush := "red")) +
>         lb$brush_handler() +
>         opts(width = 300, height = 300)
>     }
>   })
>   observe_ggvis(gv1, "plot1", session)
>
> })

ui.r
> shinyUI(bootstrapPage(
>   uiOutput("selectInputGv1X"),
>   uiOutput("selectInputGv1Y"),
>   ggvis_output("plot1")
> ))

The plots come out as expected, but trying to brush yields neither the red rectangle nor the red highlighting I expect to see. I have a feeling it may be something to do with the reactive plot data.

Does anyone have any observations on what I may be doing wrong? Any help is much appreciated.

Kevin

messages.subject_clean: Interactive plots not working, showing [object Object]
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm trying to get started with ggvis, and for me the interactive plots aren't working.  None of them.

messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone, I am a new ggvis/shiny user (with really only minimal experience with html/css/js).  I can't believe how quickly combining shiny and ggvis allowed me to make an interactive data vis app!

I apologize if this is a straightforward question but haven't been able to find an example - although i'm not sure that I am even using the right keywords.

Is it currently possible to collect id information for clicked points into a list and then send that into shiny? For example, I would love to be able to have the user select a one or more points on a scatter plot and have selected points be displayed, along with additional information in a table.  I can show this information as tool tips, but i can't figure out how to export those IDs outside of the ggvis instance.

Any help or advice would be highly appreciated.
best,

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've got something hacked together, adapted from the ggvis demos, that seems to work intermittently:

> points <- reactiveValues(selected = 1)
>
> brush_summary <- function(x) {
>
>     if(is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) return(NULL)
>     points$selected <- sapply(x, `[[`, "key__") + 1
>
>     return(paste0(" ", points$selected, ","))
>   }
>
> ggvis(mtcars, props(x = ~wt, y = ~mpg)) +
> +     layer_point(props(fillOpacity := 0.5, fillOpacity.brush := 1)) +
> +     brush_tooltip(brush_summary)

The point IDs are still put into a tooltip, since I don't know how to export the IDs without using the brush_tooltip() function, but you can also access them from points$selected.

Hope this helps! If you find out any more about how to do this brushing and getting the IDs out, I'd be happy to know more.

-Kevin
